content.title: Gauff wins nine of last 10 games to beat 16-year-old Sun, reach Beijing fourth round
content.description: Coco Gauff was pushed throughout the opening set by rising Chinese standout Sun Xinran on Monday night before pulling away late for a 7-5, 6-1 victory that sent her into the Beijing Round of 16 for the fourth straight year.

content.title: Swiatek on handmade gifts, heart-rate monitors and a hard-earned comeback
content.description: Following her three-set win over Donna Vekic, Iga Swiatek talks Beijing fan gifts, the data her team tracks in practice and the mindset behind one of her grittier wins of the season.

thumbnail.title: Swiatek on handmade gifts, heart-rate monitors and a hard-earned comeback

content.title: Hot shot: Jelena Ostapenko's pickup volley off her shoelaces in Beijing
content.description: Jelena Ostapenko's best offense was pitted against Elise Mertens' best defense in this point in the China Open third round, and it was Ostapenko who came out on top -- but she needed a spectacular volleyed pickup to get the job done in the end.

content.title: Mertens escapes Ostapenko from 2-0 down in decider; into Beijing last 16
content.description: No. 13 seed Elise Mertens made the last 16 of the China Open for the first time in her seventh appearance after defeating No. 24 seed Jelena Ostapenko 6-2, 3-6, 6-3, winning six of the last seven games from 2-0 down in the decider. The result was Mertens' first win over Ostapenko, having previously lost to the Latvian at Luxembourg 2019 (as well as one junior meeting).

content.title: Svitolina wins sixth edition of rivalry vs. Sakkari to make Beijing last 16
content.description: No. 6 seed Elina Svitolina improved to 4-2 against No. 25 seed Maria Sakkari, and 2-1 on outdoor hard courts, with a 6-4, 7-5 victory in the China Open third round.

content.title: Zheng Qinwen on surviving Beijing’s narrow margins
content.description: After another three-set win put her into the China Open last 16, Zheng Qinwen reflects on the composure and patience that have carried her through a demanding opening week at home.

thumbnail.title: BEIJING - POST-MATCH INTERVIEW - R32 - QINWEN ZHENG_Digital Download_m52357

content.title: Iga Swiatek on turning anger into a Beijing comeback
content.description: Down 6-4, 5-2 to Donna Vekic, Iga Swiatek explains how a flash of frustration sharpened her focus and helped carry her into the China Open last 16.

thumbnail.title: BEIJING - POST-MATCH INTERVIEW - R32 - IGA SWIATEK - ENGLISH_Digital Download_m52342

content.title: Hot shot: Marie Bouzkova covers the court in Beijing, finds the counterdrop
content.description: Marie Bouzkova was everywhere in this point against Zheng Qinwen in the China Open third round, ultimately sprinting up to flick a neat counterdrop past the home player for a winner.

content.title: Zheng wins third straight Beijing three-setter, quells Bouzkova in 2:54
content.description: Wild card Zheng Qinwen won her third three-setter in as many matches so far at the China Open to reach the fourth round, edging No. 18 seed Marie Bouzkova 7-6(4), 4-6, 7-5 in 2 hours and 54 minutes.

content.title: Li improves to 2-0 against Bencic to reach Beijing fourth round
content.description: No. 21 seed Ann Li improved to 2-0 against Belinda Bencic, and 4-0 in sets, with a 6-4, 6-3 defeat of the No. 9 seed in the China Open third round. Li advanced to the fourth round at WTA 1000 level for the second time in 2026 (following Madrid).

content.title: Charaeva backs up Rybakina upset by defeating Kartal in Beijing
content.description: Two days after stunning World No. 1 Elena Rybakina at the China Open, Alina Charaeva backed up the upset by defeating 2025 quarterfinalist Sonay Kartal 6-4, 6-1 to reach the fourth round of a WTA 1000 event for the first time.

content.title: Hot shot: Kamilla Rakhimova finds the angle at full stretch in Beijing
content.description: Kamilla Rakhimova soaked up both heavy blows and awkward spins from Iva Jovic in this point in the China Open third round, gradually out-maneuvering the American into a battle of angles -- which Rakhimova won with a neat backhand hook into the open space.

content.title: Jovic saves two set points, denies Rakhimova to make Beijing fourth round
content.description: No. 10 seed Iva Jovic improved tp 3-0 against Kamilla Rakhimova after coming from 5-2 and double set point down in the second set to win their China Open third-round meeting 6-1, 7-5.

content.title: From a set and a break down, Swiatek rallies to beat Vekic in Beijing third round
content.description: Former champion and No. 8 seed Iga Swiatek recovered from a 6-4, 5-2 deficit to defeat No. 30 seed Donna Vekic 4-6, 7-6 (0), 6-2 and advance to the fourth round of the China Open on Monday. Swiatek, who improved to 5-0 against Vekic, will face the winner of the match between No. 10 seed Iva Jovic and Kamilla Rakhimova next.

content.title: 'The mind-reader!' Bejlek foils Osaka with superb anticipation in Beijing
content.description: Sara Bejlek's speed and anticipation were on show in this point against Naomi Osaka in the China Open third round as she retrieved the former Workd No. 1's heaviest blows -- then slotted a remarkable pass down the line for a winner.

content.title: Muchova rallies past Samsonova in late-night Beijing thriller
content.description: Karolina Muchova continued her stellar season with a late-night comeback victory in Beijing, rallying past No. 29 seed Liudmila Samsonova 4-6, 6-4, 6-2 in 2 hours and 19 minutes to reach the fourth round.

content.title: Osaka edges Bejlek in gripping two-set battle to reach Beijing fourth round
content.description: Former World No. 1 Naomi Osaka battled past No. 20 seed Sara Bejlek in a tightly contested two-set match Sunday, earning a 7-6 (4), 6-4 victory in just over two hours to advance to the fourth round in Beijing.

content.title: Snigur routs Preston in 47 minutes in Beijing; into first WTA 1000 Round of 16
content.description: Daria Snigur booked her place in the fourth round of a WTA 1000 tournament for the first time in her career with a 6-1, 6-0 defeat of Taylah Preston in just 47 minutes.

content.title: Noskova speeds past Golubic in 55 minutes, returns to Beijing fourth round
content.description: No. 5 seed and 2025 China Open finalist Linda Noskova returned to the fourth round after defeating Viktorija Golubic 6-2, 6-1 in 55 minutes -- her second straight-sets win over the Swiss player in as many meetings in 2026.

content.title: Hot shot: Ekaterina Alexandrova's slice surprise in Beijing
content.description: Is it Ekaterina Alexandrova or is it Tatjana Maria on court at the China Open? Alexandrova took Diana Shnaider by complete surprise in this point in their third-round tilt by breaking up a power baseline exchange with a short-angled backhand slice winner, casually flicked as though it was routine. Down a set and a break, it also sparked a comeback from Alexandrova as she roared back to win the match.

content.title: Alexandrova denies Shnaider from a set and a break down in Beijing
content.description: No. 19 seed Ekaterina Alexandrova improved to 3-1 against No. 11 seed Diana Shnaider after coming from a set and 2-0 down to win their China Open third-round encounter 3-6, 6-4, 6-3. Alexandrova advanced to the last 16 in Beijing for the first time.

content.title: Andreeva eases past Polina Kudermetova to make Beijing last 16
content.description: No. 4 seed Mirra Andreeva improved to 2-0 against Polina Kudermetova with a 6-4, 6-1 win in the China Open third round.

content.title: Bartunkova upsets Sabalenka in Beijing for first career Top 3 win
content.description: No. 26 seed Nikola Bartunkova scored the second Top 10 win of her career, and the first over a Top 3 player, with a 6-4, 6-3 upset of No. 2 seed Aryna Sabalenka in the China Open third round. Bartunkova had lost to Sabalenka from 6-2, 4-0 up in their only previous meeting in this year's Berlin quarterfinals.

content.title: Kraus' breakthrough week continues with third-round win over Yastremska
content.description: Austria's Sinja Kraus advanced to the round of 16 at a WTA 1000 event for the first time in her career with a 6-4, 6-1 win over Ukraine's Dayana Yastremska. Kraus will next face No. 26 seed Nikola Bartunkova, who beat her in their only previous meeting on tour.

content.title: Beijing stunner: Charaeva spoils Rybakina's debut as World No. 1
content.description: No. 118 Alina Charaeva pulled off a stunning late-night upset in Beijing on Saturday, storming back from a set down to defeat new World No. 1 Elena Rybakina 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 in 2 hours, 11 minutes and advance to the China Open third round.

content.title: Kartal dispatches home favorite Wang Xinyu in straight sets to advance in Beijing
content.description: Competing in her first main draw since Indian Wells in March, Sonay Kartal continued her impressive return with a 6-3, 6-2 victory over No. 31 seed Wang Xinyu in 1 hour and 19 minutes to reach the third round in Beijing.

content.title: Bouzkova edges Birrell in tight two-setter to reach Beijing third round
content.description: No. 18 seed Marie Bouzkova handled business in her Beijing opener Saturday, defeating Seoul champion Kimberly Birrell 6-4, 6-4 in 1 hour and 24 minutes to reach the third round and book a showdown with home favorite Zheng Qinwen.

content.title: Sun Xinran, 16, stuns Bucsa in Beijing for first Top 50 win; to face Gauff next
content.description: Junior World No. 1 Sun Xinran continued her home-soil breakthrough at the China Open on Saturday, The 16-year-old wild card came from a break down in the second set to upset No. 27 seed Cristina Bucsa 6-4, 7-5, notching her first career Top 50 win and becoming the first 2010-born player to reach the third round of a WTA 1000 event. She will next face No. 3 seed Coco Gauff.

content.title: Jovic survives Dart in 2:45 Beijing marathon to make third round
content.description: No. 10 seed Iva Jovic battled for 2 hours and 45 minutes to defeat qualifier Harriet Dart 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 in the China Open second round. The American teenager will next face Kamilla Rakhimova.

content.title: Zheng reaches Beijing third round after Kalinskaya retires
content.description: Wild card Zheng Qinwen reached the third round of the China Open for the third straight year after No. 15 seed Anna Kalinskaya was forced to retire due to illness trailing 6-7(4), 6-4, 3-0 in the second round.

content.title: Rakhimova tops Singapore champ Fernandez in Beijing; second Top 30 win of 2026
content.description: Kamilla Rakhimova ended Singapore champion Leylah Fernandez's winning streak 6-2, 4-6, 6-3 in the China Open second round, levelling her head-to-head with the No. 23 seed at one win apiece. The result was Rakhimova's fourth career Top 30 win, and second in the past five weeks following her upset of Barbora Krejcikova in the US Open first round.

content.title: Bencic overturns 4-2 second-set deficit to beat Zakharova in Beijing
content.description: No. 9 seed Belinda Bencic scored her first win since reaching the Toronto quarterfinals in August after coming from 4-2 down in the second set to defeat Anastasia Zakharova 6-1, 7-6(3) in the China Open second round.

content.title: In first Beijing match since 2019, Svitolina bests Siniakova in three sets
content.description: In her first China Open appearance since 2019, No. 6 seed and 2016 semifinalist Elina Svitolina came from a set down to defeat Katerina Siniakova 1-6, 6-4, 6-2 in 2 hours and 1 minute in the 2026 second round. Svitolina improved to 6-0 against Siniakova -- five of her wins have come in three sets, and the sixth was a retirement.

content.title: Swiatek beats Gao, sets up Vekic clash in Beijing
content.description: No. 8 seed Iga Swiatek advanced to the third round of the China Open in Beijing with a 6-2, 6-3 win over local wild card Xinyu Gao. Swiatek will next face No. 30 seed Donna Vekic, whom she has beaten in all four of their previous meetings.

content.title: Ostapenko denies Badosa in Beijing from 5-3 down in both sets
content.description: No. 24 seed Jelena Ostapenko found her best power shots when behind in the China Open second round against Paula Badosa, coming from 5-3 down in both sets to defeat the Spaniard 7-6(5), 7-5. Ostapenko improved to 4-2 overall against Badosa, including 2-1 on outdoor hard courts and 3-0 since 2023.

content.title: Hot shots: Katie Volynets' 25-shot lung-buster plus bonus pass in Beijing
content.description: Facing one of four points to go down 6-0, 4-0 in the China Open second round against Elise Mertens, Katie Volynets came out on top of a superb 25-shot line-to-line lung-buster, eventually putting it away with a drive volley. She warmed to the task of her comeback in the second set, finding a brilliant backhand pass on the run a few games later on the way to forcing a decider.

content.title: From 6-0, 3-0 up, Mertens takes scenic route to subdue Volynets in Beijing
content.description: No. 13 seed Elise Mertens held four points to take a 6-0, 4-0 lead over Katie Volynets in the China Open -- but wound up having to come from a break down in the third set to quell the valiant American 6-0, 4-6, 7-5 in 2 hours and 54 minutes. Mertens improved to 2-0 overall against Volynets, and will next face No. 24 seed Jelena Ostapenko.

content.title: Former champ Gauff quells Osorio in three sets to make Beijing third round
content.description: A first-time encounter in the China Open second round saw No. 3 seed and 2024 champion Coco Gauff defeat Camila Osorio 7-6(4), 4-6, 6-2 in 2 hours and 18 minutes.

content.title: Hot shot: Coco Gauff shows off deft touch at net in Beijing
content.description: Coco Gauff and Camila Osorio put on a show for the China Open crowd in this exchange in their second-round tilt -- both players slid all over the court and found the deftest of angles, but it was Gauff's touch on the backhand volley that won her the point.

content.title: Sakkari storms past Hunter to reach Beijing third round
content.description: No. 25 seed Maria Sakkari broke Australian qualifier Storm Hunter six times to score a 6-2, 6-2 win in the second round of the China Open in Beijing on Saturday. Sakkari, who improved to 2-0 against Hunter, will face the winner of the match between No. 6 seed Elina Svitolina and Katerina Siniakova.

content.title: Vekic extends perfect record against Zhu to reach Beijing third round
content.description: No. 30 seed Donna Vekic improved to 4-0 against local wild card Lin Zhu with a 6-1, 4-6, 6-2 victory in the second round of the China Open in Beijing on Saturday. Vekic will next face No. 8 seed Iga Swiatek or China's Xinyu Gao for a spot in the round of 16.

content.title: Li improves to 2-0 against Krueger with Beijing win
content.description: No. 21 seed Ann Li defeated fellow American Ashlyn Krueger 6-4, 6-2 to advance to the third round of the China Open in Beijing on Saturday. Li improved to 2-0 in her head-to-head record against Krueger and will next face No. 9 seed Belinda Bencic or Anastasia Zakharova.

content.title: How tactical variety helped Zheng Qinwen escape a tricky opener in Beijing

content.title: Why carrying the top ranking in Beijing feels different for Elena Rybakina
content.description: Now the mark everyone is chasing at the China Open, Elena Rybakina is learning to soak in the moment, embracing the responsibility of the No. 1 spot and the new connections that come with it.

thumbnail.title: BEIJING - PRE-TOURNAMENT INTERVIEW - ELENA RYBAKINA_Digital Download_m52229

content.title: Sabalenka handles business in Beijing opener with decisive win over Zarazua
content.description: Aryna Sabalenka made a commanding return to action on Friday in Beijing, cruising past Renata Zarazua 6-1, 6-3 in just 62 minutes to reach the second round. The World No. 2 finished with 36 winners, surpassing Zarazua's 34 total points won.

content.title: Osaka defeats Timofeeva in three-set Beijing rollercoaster
content.description: No. 12 seed and 2019 champion Naomi Osaka came through a top-quality three-setter against Maria Timofeeva in the China Open second round, and will next face No. 20 seed Sara Bejlek for the first time.

metadata.credit: Pedro PARDO / AFP via Getty Images

content.title: Bartunkova drops just four games vs. Frech to make Beijing third round
content.description: No. 26 seed Nikola Bartunkova enjoyed a victorious China Open debut, improving to 2-0 against Magdalena Frech with a 6-2, 6-2 second-round win.

content.title: Hot shots: Moments of brilliance propel Bejlek past Inglis in Beijing
content.description: Sara Bejlek produced a pair of standout highlights in her Beijing opener, uncorking a running forehand lob in the first set before topping it early in the second with a grueling rally capped by a deft backhand drop shot and forehand putaway en route to a straight-sets victory.

content.title: On Beijing debut, Bejlek holds off Inglis to make third round
content.description: Sara Bejlek made a winning start to her first Beijing appearance Friday, with the No. 20 seed defeating Australia's Maddison Inglis 6-3, 7-5 in 1 hour and 33 minutes to reach the third round. A potential clash with Naomi Osaka awaits.

content.title: Polina Kudermetova edges Tauson in three sets to make Beijing third round
content.description: Polina Kudermetova notched her second Top 50 win of 2026 on Friday in Beijing, battling past No. 32 seed Clara Tauson 6-4, 4-6, 6-4 in just over two hours to advance to the third round.

content.title: Muchova maintains perfect record vs. Boulter to make Beijing third round
content.description: No. 7 seed Karolina Muchova improved to 3-0 against Katie Boulter (and 6-0 in sets) with a 7-6(3), 6-1 win in the China Open second round after trailing 4-1 in the first set. All three of their meetings have come in 2026 -- Muchova was also victorious in the Miami third round and US Open second round.

content.title: Snigur pulls off comeback vs. Paolini in Beijing; third Top 20 win of 2026
content.description: Daria Snigur came from a set and a break down to defeat No. 14 Jasmine Paolini 3-6, 7-6(5), 6-2 in the China Open second round, improving to 3-2 against Top 20 opponents in 2026 and 6-4 in her career.

content.title: 'Say what?!' Muchova pulls off 360-degree pickup and pass in Beijing
content.description: Come for the 360-degree spinning pickup, stay for the angled pass at full stretch: Karolina Muchova was at it again with the absurd hot shots in the China Open second round against Katie Boulter. "I'm everywhere, I'm so Karolina," as "360" singer Charli xcx might have put it.

content.title: Alexandrova improves to 6-1 vs. Sasnovich with Beijing second-round win
content.description: No. 19 seed Ekaterina Alexandrova improved to 6-1 overall (and 2-0 on outdoor hard courts) against qualifier Aliaksandra Sasnovich with a 6-1, 6-4 victory in the China Open second round. Alexandrova had to hold off a late charge by Sasnovich from 4-1 down in the second set.

content.title: Hot shots: Two magic forehand flicks by Ekaterina Alexandrova in Beijing
content.description: Ekaterina Alexandrova pulled off some magic to get herself out of trouble twice against Aliaksandra Sasnovich in the China Open second round -- at full stretch, she found the sharpest of angles on forehand squash shot winners.

content.title: From 5-2 down, Preston upsets Parry in Beijing; into first WTA 1000 Round 3
content.description: Taylah Preston notched her second career Top 30 win after coming from 5-2 down in the first set to defeat No. 22 seed Diane Parry 7-6(4), 6-1 in the China Open second round. The Australian advanced to the third round of a WTA 1000 event for the first time in her career.

content.title: Hot shots: Two pinpoint half-volleyed lobs by Linda Noskova in Beijing
content.description: Linda Noskova is known for her power, but the Wimbledon champion brought some delicate touch with two perfectly weighted lobs -- picked up on the half-volley, no less -- in the China Open second round against Elena-Gabriela Ruse.

content.title: Noskova avenges Bad Homburg loss to Ruse with win in Beijing
content.description: Last year's runner-up Linda Noskova avenged her loss to Romania's Elena-Gabriela Ruse earlier this year with a 6-4, 6-1 win to advance to the third round of the China Open in Beijing on Friday. Noskova will next face Switzerland's Viktorija Golubic for a spot in the round of 16.

content.title: From 3-1 down in decider, Samsonova escapes Linda Fruhvirtova in Beijing
content.description: No. 29 seed and 2023 runner-up Liudmila Samsonova came from 3-1 down in the third set to defeat lucky loser Linda Fruhvirtova 6-2, 3-6, 6-3 in 2 hours and 42 minutes in the China Open second round.

content.title: Golubic overcomes Stearns in three sets to make Beijing third round
content.description: Viktorija Golubic defeated No. 28 seed Peyton Stearns 6-4, 3-6, 6-3 in the China Open second round, avenging a first-round loss to the American in Miami in their only previous meeting. Golubic advances to the third round at WTA 1000 level or above for the third time in 2026 (following Rome, Roland Garros and Toronto) and for the first time in her career in Beijing.

content.title: Yastremska upsets Chwalinska to reach third round in Beijing
content.description: Ukraine's Dayana Yastremska upset No. 17 seed Maja Chwalinska, the French Open runner-up, 6-3, 6-1 to advance to the third round of the China Open in Beijing on Friday. Yastremska will next face Austria's Sinja Kraus, who advanced after Anastasia Potapova retired while trailing 4-1 in the first set of their second-round match.

content.title: Andreeva blanks Yuan in last two sets to reach Beijing third round
content.description: No. 4 seed Mirra Andreeva ralled from a set down to blank Yue Yuan in the last two sets to reach the third round of the China Open in Beijing on Friday. Andreeva scored a 3-6, 6-0, 6-0 victory and will next face No. 32 seed Clara Tauson or Polina Kudermetova.

content.title: Shnaider defeats Tjen to reach Beijing third round
content.description: No. 11 seed Diana Shnaider defeated Indonesia's Janice Tjen 6-0, 6-4 on Friday to advance to the third round of the China Open in Beijing. She will next face No. 19 seed Ekaterina Alexandrova or Aliaksandra Sasnovich for a spot in the fourth round.

content.title: Wild card Gao upsets Udvardy in Beijing for first career WTA 1000 win
content.description: Wild card Gao Xinyu upset Panna Udvardy 6-2, 6-3 in the China Open first round to claim her fourth career Top 100 win (and first since beating Beatriz Haddad Maia at the 2025 United Cup), and first main-draw victory at WTA 1000 level. The 28-year-old will next face No. 8 seed and 2023 champion Iga Swiatek.

content.title: Osorio bests Tararudee in Beijing first round; to face Gauff next
content.description: Camila Osorio snapped a four-match losing streak to defeat Lanlana Tararudee 6-3, 6-3 in the China Open first round, setting a second-round meeting with No. 3 seed and 2024 champion Coco Gauff.

content.title: Valerie Camillo explains how the 2027 calendar will strengthen the WTA Tour
content.description: WTA Chair Valerie Camillo discusses a calendar shaped by player and tournament input, the push for greater flexibility and the equal prize money milestone arriving at every combined WTA 1000 event.

content.title: Hot shots: Sun Xinran, 16, thrills Beijing crowd with both power and touch
content.description: Sun Xinran, the 16-year-old junior No. 1, went toe-to-toe with Eva Lys in a succession of high-octane baseline battles in the China Open first round. At 2-1, she switched up the power exchange brilliantly on the 22nd stroke with a clean drop shot winner. Three games later, she fired an off backhand bullet straight into the corner on the 23rd stroke. "Is there anything she can't do?" marvelled the commentator.

content.title: Hot shots: Two brilliant winners on the run by Harriet Dart in Beijing
content.description: Never stop scampering: Harriet Dart's footspeed paid off in the China Open first round against Qu Yihan in two brilliant rallies -- the first a line-to-line exchange that the Briton finished with a forehand down the line on the run, and the second a deftly angled counterdrop.

content.title: Junior No. 1 Sun Xinran advances in WTA debut in Beijing as Lys retires
content.description: 16-year-old Sun Xinran, the US Open junior champion and junior World No. 1, won her WTA main-draw debut after Eva Lys was forced to retire due to a foot injury trailing 6-1, 3-0 in the China Open first round. The Chinese teenager advances to face No. 27 seed Cristina Bucsa.

content.title: Dart survives stern test by 17-year-old Qu in 3:03 Beijing thriller
content.description: Qualifier Harriet Dart battled past 17-year-old Chinese wild card Qu Yihan 6-2, 6-7(5), 7-5 in 3 hours and 3 minutes in the China Open first round, recovering after coming within two points of victory in the second set. Junior No. 19 Qu, ranked No. 1,297 on the WTA, was making her WTA main-draw debut. Dart will next face No. 10 seed Iva Jovic for the first time.

content.title: Hot shot: Qu Yihan dives for a lob, stretches for a volley in Beijing
content.description: Qu Yihan showed off her range on her WTA debut as she pushed Harriet Dart all the way in the China Open first round -- especially in this point, where the 17-year-old turned the point around with a superb lob before finishing it with an exquisite volley at full stretch.

content.title: Zhu tops Parks on home soil in Beijing for first WTA win in 12 months
content.description: Wild card Zhu Lin improved to 2-1 against Alycia Parks with a 6-4, 6-2 victory in the China Open first round -- the 32-year-old's first tour-level win since reaching the 2025 Ningbo quarterfinals. Zhu will next face No. 30 seed Donna Vekic.

content.title: Hot shot: Zakharova slides to perfection to hit forehand winner
content.description: Anastasia Zakharova hit a stunning forehand winner after sliding to perfection during her first-round match against local wild card Yushan Shao at the China Open in Beijing on Thursday.

content.title: Rakhimova holds off Bassols Ribera to reach Beijing second round
content.description: Kamilla Rakhimova recovered after losing three straight games from 5-3 up in the second set to defeat qualifier Marina Bassols Ribera 6-4, 7-6(2) in the China Open first round. Rakhimova advances to face No. 23 seed and last week's Singapore champion Leylah Fernandez.

content.title: On fourth match point, Zakharova quells 17-year-old wild card Shao in Beijing
content.description: Anastasia Zakharova needed four match points to seal victory over 17-year-old Chinese wild card Shao Yushan in the China Open first round, but got over the line in 59 minutes to set up a second-round meeting with No. 9 seed Belinda Bencic. Shao, a former junior No. 17 currently ranked No. 752 on the WTA, was making her WTA main-draw debut.

content.title: Hunter defeats 16-year-old wild card Lin in 66-minute Beijing opener
content.description: Qualifier Storm Hunter advanced 6-2, 6-1 against 16-year-old Chinese wild card Lin Yu-Jun in the China Open first round. Lin, the junior No. 24 and WTA No. 1,015, was making her WTA main-draw debut. Hunter will next face No. 25 seed Maria Sakkari.

content.title: Two points from defeat, Badosa escapes Kasatkina in Beijing opener
content.description: Paula Badosa defeated Daria Kasatkina for the second time in five weeks in the China Open first round, reprising her US Open first-round win with a 4-6, 7-6(7), 6-4 victory in 2 hours and 38 minutes. Badosa, who had trailed 5-2 in the second-set tiebreak, improved to 5-4 overall (and 3-2 on outdoor hard courts) against Kasatkina. The Spaniard will next face No. 24 seed Jelena Ostapenko, who leads their head-to-head 3-2.

content.title: Siniakova wins sixth edition of rivalry vs. Linette in Beijing opener
content.description: Katerina Siniakova came from 4-2 down in the first set to defeat Magda Linette 6-4, 6-3 in the China Open first round, levelling their head-to-head at three wins apiece. Linette won their first three meetings between 2012 and 2019, but Siniakova has won the most recent three since 2022.

content.title: Hot shot: Stretched Charaeva passes Starodubtseva with down-the-line backhand
content.description: Stretched out wide, Alina Charaeva passes Yuliia Starodubtseva with a backhand winner down the line during her three-set win in the first round of the China Open in Beijing on Thursday.

content.title: Seoul champion Birrell continues winning ways in Beijing
content.description: Kimberly Birrell, who won the Korea Open title in Seoul last week, extended her winning streak to six matches with a 6-1, 6-1 victory over Japan’s Aoi Ito at the China Open in Beijing. Birrell will next face No. 18 seed Marie Bouzkova, whom she defeated in their only previous meeting on the professional tour.

content.title: Charaeva overhauls Starodubtseva in 3:12 first-round marathon in Beijing
content.description: Alina Charaeva came from a set and a break down to defeat Yuliia Starodubtseva in the China Open first round, scoring her first career WTA 1000 win and her third Top 50 victory. The Armenian No. 1 will next face No. 1 seed Elena Rybakina.

content.title: Zheng battles past qualifier Shi in all-Chinese first-round Beijing derby
content.description: A battle of home players in the China Open first round saw wild card Zheng Qinwen overcome qualifier Shi Han 7-6(6), 4-6, 6-2 in 2 hours and 44 minutes after coming from a break down in the first set. Zheng improved to 6-1 at tour-level against her Chinese compatriots, while Shi won a set from a Top 100 player for the first time in seven meetings.

content.title: Kartal eases past Lazaro Garcia in Beijing for first win of injury comeback
content.description: Sonay Kartal won her first match since reaching the fourth round of Indian Wells in March, defeating Spanish qualifier Andrea Lazaro Garcia 6-2, 6-3 in the China Open first round. Kartal was sidelined for six months following Indian Wells due to a back injury; she returned to action at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals in the week before Beijing, losing her first match back to Marie Bouzkova.

content.title: Volynets edges Montgomery in two tight sets, wins all-American Beijing derby
content.description: In a first-time encounter between two American compatriots, Katie Volynets edged qualifier Robin Montgomery 7-5, 7-5 in the China Open first round. Volynets will next face No. 13 seed Elise Mertens.

content.title: Zarazua throws kitchen sink at Bondar to earn clutch break in Beijing
content.description: Renata Zarazua trailed 5-3 in the opening set of her first-round match against Anna Bondar in Beijing on Wednesday but stormed back, using every shot in her arsenal to win this pivotal 17-shot rally and secure a clutch break.

content.title: Watch: Maja Chwalinska turn a moonball into September Shot of the Month
Zarazua saves three set points, reverses Seoul loss to Bondar in Beijing
content.description: Renata Zarazua saved three set points trailing 5-3 in the first set, then roared back to defeat Anna Bondar 7-6(4), 6-3 in the China Open first round, reversing her 2-6, 6-3, 6-1 loss to the Hungarian at the same stage of Seoul the previous week. Zarazua will next face No. 2 seed Aryna Sabalenka, to whom she lost 6-4, 6-0 in their only previous meeting at Brisbane 2024.

content.title: Frech outlasts Jacquemot in 2:43 Beijing first-round nightcap
content.description: Magdalena Frech improved to 4-1 overall against Elsa Jacquemot after quelling the French qualifier 7-5, 3-6, 6-4 in 2 hours and 43 minutes in the China Open first round. This was the first of their meetings to go to three sets; Frech had won 6-4, 6-0 in the Hobart first round in January in their most recent encounter.

content.title: Dream big, play big: Shared values, great friends and the heart of a tennis player
Boulter advances past Hontama in Beijing, sets Muchova rematch
content.description: Katie Boulter improved to 2-0 against qualifier Mai Hontama with a 6-3, 6-4 win in the China Open first round, overturning a 2-0 deficit in the second set. She will face No. 7 seed and 2024 finalist Karolina Muchova in the second round for the third time in 2026, having lost to the Czech in straight sets in the Miami third round and US Open second round.

content.title: Preston saves two set points, defeats Korpatsch in Beijing opener
content.description: Taylah Preston saved two set points trailing 5-4 in the second set to defeat Tamara Korpatsch 6-2, 7-6(4) in the China Open first round.

content.title: On home soil, Yuan passes Oliynykova test to make Beijing second round
content.description: Wild card Yuan Yue defeated Oleksandra Oliynykova 6-2, 6-3 in the China Open first round -- her first tour-level win since Charleston in April and her first Top 50 win since defeating Diana Shnaider in the second round of Cincinnati 2025.

content.title: Lucky loser Linda Fruhvirtova takes second chance, bests Bai in Beijing
content.description: Lucky loser Linda Fruhvirtova defeated qualifier Bai Zhuoxuan 6-2, 6-3 in the China Open first round to notch her first tour-level win since reaching the Ostrava quarterfinals in February.

content.title: Inglis upsets Sonmez in Beijing for first tour-level win since January
content.description: Qualifier Maddison Inglis came from 3-1 down in the first set, then converted her sixth match point in the second to defeat Zeynep Sonmez 6-4, 6-4 in the China Open first round. The result was Inglis's first Top 100 win since beating Alycia Parks in Queen's qualifying, and her first tour-level win since the Australian Open in January.

content.title: Sasnovich cruises past Singapore finalist Gibson in Beijing opener
content.description: Qualifier Aliaksandra Sasnovich improved to 2-0 against Singapore finalist Talia Gibson with a 6-1, 6-4 victory in the China Open first round. The result was Sasnovich's first win at WTA 1000 level since making the third round of Beijing the previous year.

content.title: Hot shot: Snigur opens court with angled backhand before hitting forehand winner
content.description: Daria Snigur opened up the court with a sharp, angled backhand against Katarzyna Kawa before finishing the incredible rally with a forehand winner during their first-round clash at the China Open.

content.title: Hot shot: Sasnovich has 'the last laugh' after winning backhand exchange
content.description: Aliaksandra Sasnovich went backhand-to-backhand with Talia Gibson during this rally in their first-round clash at the China Open before ending it with a delightful drop-shot winner.

content.title: Snigur escapes Kawa from 3-0 down in decider to reach Beijing second round
content.description: Daria Snigur improved to 2-0 against Katarzyna Kawa after coming from 3-0 down in the third set to win 3-6, 6-4, 7-5 in the China Open first round. Snigur previously defeated Kawa 6-1, 2-6, 6-2 in Australian Open qualifying in January.

content.title: Polina Kudermetova overcomes lucky loser Ma in three-set Beijing opener
content.description: After losing the first set from a break up, Polina Kudermetova recovered to defeat Chinese lucky loser Ma Yexin in three sets in the China Open first round. The win was Kudermetova's first at WTA 1000 level or above since the Australian Open in January.

content.title: Golubic sets up second-round clash with Stearns at China Open
content.description: Switzerland’s Viktorija Golubic defeated lucky loser Elvina Kalieva 6-3, 6-1 to advance to the second round of the China Open in Beijing. Golubic will next face No. 28 seed Peyton Stearns for a place in the third round.
